alerts.title: Untreated hypothyroidism mimics DTG weight gain
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L with low Free T4, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, delayed ankle reflexes, constipation, cold intolerance, and fatigue — classic hypothyroidism. She often forgets her levothyroxine. The clinician attributes 9 kg weight gain to DTG and plans to switch, but inadequately treated hypothyroidism is a compelling alternative cause. Correcting levothyroxine adherence and dose should be attempted before attributing weight gain solely to DTG. Switching away from DTG prematurely risks losing a well-tolerated, high-genetic-barrier regimen with suppressed viral load.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise levothyroxine adherence and dose, recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks before attributing weight gain to DTG or switching ART.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycemia risk factors present
alerts.message: Guidelines list risk factors for DTG-associated hyperglycemia: age ≥30, BMI ≥25 kg/m², family history of DM, and hypertension. This patient is 45 and has BMI 33, meeting two risk factors. Guidelines state clients with ≥2 risk factors and normal baseline glucose should have RBS or FBS monitored every 3 months for 6 months. Current fasting glucose 5.6 mmol/L is normal, but no evidence of prior serial glucose monitoring exists. The dyslipidemia pattern (LDL 4.2, total cholesterol 6.4, triglycerides 2.3) further supports metabolic risk that compounds DTG hyperglycemia concern.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor fasting or random blood glucose every 3 months for 6 months given two hyperglycemia risk factors on DTG.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue by 2 months
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for experienced patients on TDF. The last creatinine was 196 days ago (2025-08-12), so the annual check is not yet overdue. However, no eGFR was recorded alongside the creatinine. The clinician's plan includes no renal monitoring orders today. Given the patient's rising BMI and metabolic abnormalities, ensuring complete renal screening per protocol is advisable. Creatinine 72 umol/L was normal, providing reassurance against current renal dysfunction.

evidence.recommended_action: Ensure eGFR is calculated with creatinine at next visit; continue annual TDF renal monitoring per guidelines.
